statements.quote: In 2025, we benefited from substantial improvements in DRAM pricing, volumes and margins as compared to 2024, reflecting strong demand growth, driven in part by the continued advancement of AI.
statements.notes: Links DRAM pricing and volume gains (and so revenue) to AI demand in words only; revenue is implied rather than named.

statements.quote: During 2025, we shifted a portion of our DRAM supply to the data center and hyperscale cloud markets to meet the strong demand fueled by AI, with emphasis on HBM products, resulting in a revenue mix weighted more prominently toward segments experiencing higher growth.
statements.notes: Revenue mix shifted toward AI, data-center and HBM demand; no AI or HBM revenue amount or share is stated.

statements.quote: •CMBU revenue increased 257% primarily due to increases in DRAM bit shipments and average selling prices driven by accelerating AI demand in cloud server markets for HBM, high-capacity dual in-line memory modules (“DIMMS”), and low-power server DRAM.
statements.notes: 257% is segment revenue growth, not a share of revenue from AI, so recorded as qualitative. Segment revenue (CMBU) has AI demand as its primary driver. No year in the sentence; context is fiscal 2025.

statements.quote: During 2025, CMBU revenue benefited from a shift of our DRAM supply to meet the strong demand in high-value data center markets.
statements.notes: Data-center demand is named as a driver of segment revenue; no amount is attributed to it.

statements.quote: •CDBU revenue increased 45% primarily due to increases in average selling prices for both data center DRAM and NAND and NAND bit shipments due to increased demand for data center SSDs.
statements.notes: 45% is segment revenue growth, not a share of revenue from data centers. The driver is data-center demand rather than AI explicitly. No year in the sentence; context is fiscal 2025.
